concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
question: Which element is located in Group 18 of the periodic table and is known for its lack of chemical reactivity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Helium** is a chemical element and is part of **Group 18** (Noble Gases) in the **Periodic Table**.
 
• It is known for its **inertness** due to its full valence electron shell, making it highly stable and almost non-reactive under normal conditions.
 
• **Helium** has **two protons** and is represented by the symbol **He**.
 
• It is the **second-lightest** and **second-most abundant element** in the universe, following hydrogen.
 
• Helium is a **colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas** at room temperature and is widely used for applications requiring non-reactivity, such as in balloons, cryogenics, and as a protective gas in welding.
 
• Its **low boiling point** (-268.93°C) makes it useful in applications like cooling superconducting magnets in MRI machines.
 
• As a noble gas, helium has **no tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons**, which explains its lack of chemical reactivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Oxygen**__

 __
 
• **Oxygen** is a highly reactive element and belongs to **Group 16** of the periodic table, also known as the chalcogens.
 
• It is essential for **respiration** in living organisms and is a part of the Earth's atmosphere (~21%).
 
• Oxygen readily forms compounds, such as water (H₂O), due to its high electronegativity.
 
• It is not inert and reacts with many elements and compounds.
 
 
 
• ** Chlorine**__
 __
 
• **Chlorine** is a highly reactive halogen belonging to **Group 17** of the periodic table.
 
• It is widely used as a **disinfectant** and in the production of **plastics** like PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• Chlorine forms compounds such as sodium chloride (common salt) and is not chemically inert.
 
 
 
• ** Fluorine**__
 
 
• **Fluorine** is the most reactive element in the periodic table and belongs to **Group 17** (halogens).
 
• It has a high electronegativity, which makes it highly reactive with most elements, including some noble gases under specific conditions.
 
• Fluorine compounds, such as fluoride, are widely used in toothpaste and water fluoridation to prevent dental cavities.
